rationale: Comparison for unit:meta.lean.definitions.navigation against rust:mdbook-dada/src/lean.rs:read_source, rust:mdbook-dada/src/lean.rs:extract_declaration, rust:mdbook-dada/src/lean.rs:select, rust:mdbook-dada/src/lean.rs:highlighted, test:mdbook-dada/tests/book.rs:authored_grammar_rejects_invalid_citations_and_missing_bodies, test:mdbook-dada/tests/book.rs:linked_examples_fail_on_invalid_citations_bodies_or_nesting, test:mdbook-dada/tests/book.rs:authored_theorems_select_literal_qualified_names, test:mdbook-dada/src/lean.rs:tests::qualified_theorem_names_match_only_the_literal_declaration_name, test:mdbook-dada/src/lean.rs:tests::definitions_reject_unsupported_incomplete_and_ambiguous_sources, test:mdbook-dada/tests/renderer_contracts.rs:lean_citations_accept_subdirectories_but_reject_source_root_escapes. read_source accepts relative .lean paths and omitted extensions, canonicalizes to enforce containment including symlinks, and reports missing sources. The cited tests exercise subdirectories, traversal/absolute/symlink escapes, qualified names, missing/wrong-kind targets and malformed bodies. No claim of a standalone or elaborated excerpt is made. limitations: Author self-review, not an independent fresh reviewer.

Lean checks proof correctness separately. Tooling review checks implementation and finite test coverage, not universal correctness or browser/CDN behavior. Additional context keys identify supporting definitions inspected in those files, not an audit of every proof or line.
